quarterly_data.signal: CFO Yokokawa: Q4 FY2026 (April-June 2026) net sales were JPY60.9 billion, operating income JPY27.0 billion and net income JPY20.6 billion - down year on year but a significant increase quarter on quarter; quarterly service sales of JPY16.5 billion were a record. Q4 sales by region included Korea JPY16.8 billion and Taiwan JPY14.4 billion. Full-year FY2026 sales and profit were down year on year but above the company's forecast; by product, full-year sales were ACTIS JPY70.5 billion and MATRICS JPY51.2 billion, and President Sendoda said mask shops contributed slightly more of ACTIS sales, approximately 60%. Employees numbered 1,335, up roughly 170 in a year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 FY2026 net sales JPY60.9 billion; operating income JPY27.0 billion; services JPY16.5 billion (record); FY2026 ACTIS sales JPY70.5 billion, MATRICS JPY51.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 orders by product (CFO Yokokawa, President Sendoda): ACTIS JPY62.0 billion and MATRICS JPY77.2 billion. Sendoda said MATRICS drove the upside, on production expansion at the advanced 2nm and 3nm nodes, while A200HiT was still being introduced to fabs for evaluation; more ACTIS orders came from wafer fabs than from mask shops. The yen's weakening through the year had an FX impact of about JPY17.4 billion on the backlog.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 orders: ACTIS JPY62.0 billion; MATRICS JPY77.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: FY2027 (year to June 2027) forecast and order outlook (President Sendoda): record-high net sales of JPY290 billion and operating income of JPY125 billion (up JPY19.7 billion) at JPY150 to the US dollar. Orders are expected at JPY300 billion to JPY400 billion (mid-point JPY350 billion) on robust demand for mask inspection systems as logic and memory makers raise investment plans and the 1.4 nanometer node generation gets under way; MATRICS and ACTIS orders are each expected to roughly double, with MATRICS above JPY100 billion, and H1 and H2 orders at about the same level. The JPY300 billion end assumes delayed orders (a conservative view); the JPY400 billion end includes upside from additional A200HiT orders if evaluations go well. The mid-point rose from three months earlier on A300 orders added from multiple DRAM mask-shop customers and stronger MATRICS demand; all three major customers' investment appetite is getting stronger. Sendoda said that from FY2028 he thinks the strength will continue or be above that, adding that these figures have not yet been thoroughly validated. CFO Yokokawa attributed the lower forecast margin to product mix and higher R&D, planned at upwards of JPY20 billion versus JPY16.2 billion, plus slightly higher staffing costs, and said the forecast is conservative to some extent; per yen of exchange-rate movement, the impact is JPY1.1 billion on sales and JPY1.0 billion on profit.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 forecast: net sales JPY290 billion; operating income JPY125 billion; orders JPY300 billion to JPY400 billion (mid-point JPY350 billion); R&D upwards of JPY20 billion

quarterly_data.signal: ACTIS A200HiT and A300 (President Sendoda): demo evaluations of A200HiT with customer samples at Lasertec's own sites are complete with a favorable response; tools are being installed gradually at customer sites, where evaluations have not yet started. Some fabs with multiple fabs and nodes are placing first orders before the evaluation ends, used concurrently for evaluation. Additional A200HiT orders could come at the earliest at the beginning of the next calendar year (H2 of the fiscal year), and evaluation completion by the end of this calendar year would be difficult; he called the roughly JPY50 billion upside a figure not thoroughly determined. A200HiT is initially expected at the N2 node, then N3; he expects all logic fabs eventually to implement it and sees no major technical bottleneck in evaluation. A300 orders are expected from logic mask shops and leading-edge fabs (R&D, including high-NA and angstrom-generation nodes beyond N2) in H1, split about 50/50, and from DRAM mask shops around the end of Q2 into H2.
quarterly_data.figure: A200HiT additional orders at the earliest from the beginning of next calendar year

quarterly_data.signal: Other demand comments (President Sendoda): DRAM fabs are increasingly inquiring about actinic inspection because DRAM and HBM masks have large areas and multiple layers and defect tolerance is tightening; this is not yet in forecasts, and timing may depend on cleanroom additions because DRAM makers face a shortage of cleanroom space. In China, where Lasertec cannot sell EUV equipment, inquiries for MATRICS DUV equipment are very strong; he said MATRICS as a whole may roughly double. Metal-based EUV pellicles, if adopted, would be a tailwind since only ACTIS can inspect through them, but pellicles are not yet commercialized; wider use of curvilinear masks should also raise demand for ACTIS's inspection sensitivity.
